paragraphs: Wisdom sits at the door of the one who rises early, and goes about the streets herself looking for the worthy; the search, it seems, is mutual before it is anything else. The psalmist’s thirst belongs to a dry land, yet his memory of God keeps watch on his bed through the night watches. Paul will not let the sleepers be mourned as people without hope: they sleep in Jesus, and the trumpet will find no one finally alone.

In the parable the door is shut and the oil cannot be lent. That is less harsh than it sounds. What the wise carry is not a possession to be divided but a love received as a gift, kept within, and spent in works, which is how Augustine, and Benedict XVI after him, read the oil. All ten slept. What differed was the vessel.

quote.text: If you keep the usual order, it will be uppermost; if you change the order, it will be uppermost. Charity never falls.
quote.attribution: St Augustine, Sermon 43 on the New Testament Lessons (Ben. 93), on Matthew 25:1–13, §5
quote.translation: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, series 1, vol. 6 (ed. P. Schaff)

closing: A lamp may be borrowed for an evening; a love cannot. Keep filling the vessel quietly, until the cry at midnight sounds like the step of a friend.
